newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST - Australian Sports News - Feb 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Lawyers for banned Super League players Jack Elsegood and John Cross are expected to make another attempt today to allow the two to compete in the new competition this year. They will ask Justice David Hodgson to order that any Australian Rugby League (AL) contract the players signed to include the provision that they are allowed to return to their Super League clubs should the conjunction by the ARL be removed. Page 20.

As the first of the Test series is set to begin today in South Africa, the Australian cricket team has been warned by Shane Warne to be wary of the hostile homeside crowds. Warne was fined A$4000 by the Australian Cricket Board for inappropriate behavior while on tour in South Africa three years ago. Page 20.

Charlotta Sorenstam, 23, has mostly lived in sister champion golf player Annika Sorenstam's shadow. Yesterday, however, she emerged as a player in her own right firing a impressive six-under-par in the first round to share the overnight lead with 33 year old Canadian Gail Graham at the A$840,000 Alpine Australian Ladies Masters. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australian Olympic 20 km walker Nick A'Hern yesterday became one of the first Australian athletes to automatically qualify for the Athens world championships, where he hopes to win first place $US60,000 in the 20 km walk. He is also among the 10 world-class walkers invited to Mexico City to attend a international race walking festival. Page 45.

The Australian cricket team is set to play its first Test match against South Africa today, at Johannesburg. With both teams evenly matched the result will depend on the individual performances of players such as Mark Taylor and Matthew Elliott on the Australian side and Gary Kirsten and Jacques Kallis on the South African. Page 46.

The rebel Australian football competition Super League has announced it will introduce penalties for players who engage in acts such as stiff-arm tackles, punching, shoulder charges, head-butting, eye-gouging and head trampling. The penalties will include an immediate send off and a two year suspension from the competition. Page 46.
THE AGE

Melbourne is facing difficulties in remaining host of the first grand prix of the season due to the number of races increasing next year. Max Mosley, president of FIA, the governing body of grand prix racing, announced plans to increase the number of races to 19, up from three last year, threatening Melbourne's planned scheduling of the event. Page B8.

Australian athlete Shirley de la Hunty has had a long and distinguished career with several gold medals in the 80 metres hurdle in the 1952 and 1956 Olympics. Retiring in 1960 she has remained involved as administrator and coach in the sport ever since and now at 71 is coaching Sydney 2000 Olympic games hopefuls David Cooper and Manesh Pillay. Page B8.

Briton Damon Hill's defence of the world drivers championship has collapsed a week before his first grand prix of the season is due to be held at Albert Park. The front wing on his Arrows-Yamaha car collapsed during Hill's final pre-season workout in England. Page B10.
THE HERALD SUN

The premier team in the Australian Football League, Club Carlton, is today reeling from the shock news that its captain Stephen Kernahan will miss the start of the season due to a serious tendon injury to his left hand suffered in a recent match. He is lkely to be sidelined for six weeks. Page 104.

The Australian national athletic titles being held this weekend are set to see strong competition between Cathy Freeman and arch-rival Melinda Gainsford-Taylor in the 200m. Freeman has predicted that she will win - a claim greeted with scepticism by Gaisford-Taylor, the world's reigning indoor champion in the event. Page 96.

Australian sprinter Dean Capobianco is still attempting to clear his name of the drug use charges dating from the 1996 Atlanta Olympics and awaiting a decision from the international arbitration panel due to meet on March 15 which will decide if his carer continues. Meanwhile he is set to compete in the 100m and 200m races in this weekends Australian national athletic championships. Page 97.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Coverage of the Australian Super League competition by free-to-air TV Channel 7 will be limited with plans to screen the competition in prime time only in the city of origin. The matches will be re-screened in other cities during non prime time slots. Page 117.

The Australian racing industry has been rocked by jockey Greg Hall's riding tactics during the 1996 Golden Slipper race, described as "serious, dangerous and unfair" by the New South Wales Racing Appeals Tribunal. Hall has been ordered to pay a record $5,000 fine which is the maximum penalty possible under Australian racing laws. Page 120.

Former Australian Rugby League chief executive John Quayle, in his struggle against the rival Super League competition, accused them of introducing the dirty concept of profit into rugby league. It is an attitude shared by his successor Neil Whittaker as outlined in his maiden speech at the ARL's season launch last Monday night. Page 117.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-29373-1800
